label: Vector spaces, subspaces and dimension — mastery test (unseen)

items.stem: A subspace must contain:
options: Every vector in the ambient space
items.explanation: Every vector subspace contains the additive identity.

items.stem: The span of a set of vectors is:
items.explanation: The span includes every linear combination and is a subspace.

items.stem: A basis is a set that is:
items.explanation: A basis must satisfy both conditions: it spans every vector in the space and is linearly independent, so no vector is redundant.

items.stem: The dimension of R³ is:
items.explanation: The standard basis of R³ is {(1,0,0),(0,1,0),(0,0,1)}. It contains three independent vectors, so the dimension is three.
items.check: Count independent basis vectors or apply the dimension formula, keeping the given basis order.

items.stem: The dimension of P₂ is:
items.explanation: The polynomials 1, x and x² are linearly independent and span all polynomials of degree at most two. Thus dim(P₂)=3.
items.check: Count independent basis vectors or apply the dimension formula, keeping the given basis order.

items.stem: The set {(x,y):x+y=1} is:
items.explanation: The equation x+y=1 excludes (0,0), since 0+0 is not one. A vector subspace must contain the zero vector.

items.stem: The set {(x,y):y=2x} is:
items.explanation: It is a line through the origin and is closed under linear combinations.

items.stem: The span of (1,0) and (2,0) in R² has dimension:
items.explanation: The vectors are proportional and generate one line.
items.check: Count independent basis vectors or apply the dimension formula, keeping the given basis order.

items.stem: The vectors are linearly independent if:
options: Only the trivial linear combination gives zero
items.explanation: This is the defining independence condition.

items.stem: The intersection of two subspaces is:
items.explanation: It contains zero and is closed under addition and scaling.

items.stem: The union of two subspaces is:
items.explanation: The sum of a vector from each subspace may not lie in the union.

items.stem: A basis of R² has how many vectors?
items.explanation: A basis of R² has exactly two vectors because the standard basis has two independent coordinate directions and every basis has the same size.
items.check: Count independent basis vectors or apply the dimension formula, keeping the given basis order.

items.stem: Coordinates of 2−3x+4x² in basis (1,x,x²) are:
items.explanation: Read coefficients in the stated basis order.
items.check: Count independent basis vectors or apply the dimension formula, keeping the given basis order.

items.stem: If dim(U)=3, dim(W)=2 and dim(U∩W)=1, dim(U+W) is:
items.explanation: Apply dim(U+W)=dim(U)+dim(W)−dim(U∩W). Substituting 3, 2 and 1 gives 3+2−1=4.
items.check: Count independent basis vectors or apply the dimension formula, keeping the given basis order.

items.stem: Which statements about subspaces are true?
items.explanation: A, B and C are true: zero, closure and span are core subspace properties.
statements: A subspace is closed under addition
The span of any set is a subspace
The union of two subspaces is always a subspace

C.why: Linear combinations are closed under the vector operations.

items.stem: If three vectors in R² are given, they are:
items.explanation: More than two vectors in a two-dimensional space must be dependent.

items.stem: A polynomial space P₃ has dimension:
items.explanation: The standard basis is {1,x,x²,x³}, which has four elements.
items.check: Count independent basis vectors or apply the dimension formula, keeping the given basis order.

items.stem: Which statements about a basis are true?
items.explanation: Statements A, B and D are true: a basis spans, is linearly independent, and every basis of a finite-dimensional space has the same number of vectors. Redundant vectors are not allowed.
statements: A basis may contain redundant vectors
All bases of a finite-dimensional space have the same size

items.stem: If two non-zero vectors in R² are not proportional, they:
items.explanation: Two non-proportional vectors are independent and hence form a basis of R².

items.stem: The dimension of the span of (1,0,0),(0,1,0),(1,1,0) is:
items.explanation: The third vector is the sum of the first two, so only two independent directions remain.
items.check: Count independent basis vectors or apply the dimension formula, keeping the given basis order.

items.stem: For finite-dimensional subspaces, dim(U+W) equals:
items.explanation: Subtract the intersection to avoid double-counting common directions.
